newsitem.title: EAST TIMOR: Bishop proposes dialogue to end East Timor problem.
newsitem.headline: Bishop proposes dialogue to end East Timor problem.

text.p: Nobel laureate Bishop Carlos Belo on Wednesday proposed that East Timor's problems be solved by dialogue between conflicting groups.

"For an end to the problems of East Timor we propose an open dialogue between all parties, between leaders and the led (and) between political leaders," Belo told a meeting between government officials, military leaders and young people.

"The dialogue for peace must be determined to end social conflict and to struggle for general welfare," Belo told the meeting at the governor's office in Dili attended by university students and a number of youth groups. "Attention should be given to the interests of each group ... and through continuous dialogue, where there is true freedom and the use of democratic rights by all sides, a structure can appear which is more participative," Belo said in a speech.

Earlier this month, more than 109 youths were arrested in Viqueque, about 100 km (60 miles) east of Dili, after fighting between members of the military-backed Gada Paksi youth group and Catholic youths. Police say four remain in custody.

Members of Gada Paksi, the Youth Guard of Integration Upholders, were among the 500 people who attended the meeting, which was addressed by the Jakarta-appointed governor Abilio Soares and East Timor's military and police chiefs.

Young people in the mostly Catholic East Timor were at the forefront of protests late last year in support of Belo and his co-Nobel Peace prize winner, the East Timorese independence activist Jose Ramos Horta.

Youths are also active in clandestine movements and a small group of guerrillas that oppose Indonesian rule in East Timor more than 21 years after Jakarta invaded the former Portuguese territory in December 1975.
The United Nations does not recognise Indonesia's July 1976 annexation of East Timor and regards Portugal as the territory's administering power.
